body:
**The one I would fix first.** The trim escalated a claim and deleted the evidence against it in the same commit.

> Per 0x6r1an0y ... that **bricks the card permanently**: the cost is the card, not just its identity - **and the opt-in writes above reach the same blocks**.

The "same blocks" are not the same blocks. The bricking claim is about "an un-finalized gen3 card's UID registers and configuration signature" (`:105`), which live at **0x10/0x11 and 0x14/0x15** - blocks 16/17 and 20/21. The opt-in writes go to **56/57/62/63** (`:104`). On a gen3 card those four are ordinary user data, which is exactly what `iso15693_poller.c:30` says of any tag that big.

And the addresses that would let a reader check this are gone. `9b80e348` removed "keeps its UID in blocks 0x10/0x11 with a configuration signature in 0x14/0x15" from this very bullet, and `grep -rn "0x10/0x11\|0x14/0x15"` over the whole app now returns nothing. The claim became unfalsifiable in the same edit that made it stronger.

At `536e0d4f` this bullet said the weaker, correct thing: "the clone path can **damage** a gen3 card too, not only the wipe."

Two fixes, and I would take both: restore the block numbers - they are the entire content of "UID registers and configuration signature" - and put `:107` back to damage rather than brick. The wipe genuinely can brick a gen3 card because it sweeps 16/17 and 20/21 along with everything else. The gen1 opt-in cannot, because it never addresses them.

> it **re-reads the UID afterwards, where it can, and reports whether it moved**

The old wording - "reports a change rather than claiming one" - was the precise one, and the code has not changed. `iso15693_poller.c:1400-1411`: `uid_changed` is set only inside the success branch of `verify_inventory`. If the card does not come back, `uid_verified` stays false and nothing is asserted in either direction. The app reports a positive observation; it never reports the absence of one.

"reports whether it moved" promises a binary answer the code cannot produce.

`9b80e348` added the correct version to a scene in the same push, `nfc_magic_scene_write_confirm.c:49-51`:

> the wipe re-reads the UID afterwards and reports a move when it sees one. **It cannot report the absence of a move**: a card bricked past inventorying goes unreported, which is why uid_verified is a separate field.

`CHANGELOG.md:67-68` also still has it right ("UID not re-checked" rather than implying the identity was confirmed), so this line is the odd one out rather than a deliberate simplification.

The arithmetic here is nearly right, and the piece it is missing makes it under-warn. Two gates have to pass before the sweep can break, and this paragraph models only one.

```c
:947   if(++absent_run < ISO15693_POLLER_WIPE_ABSENT_RUN) continue;   // needs b >= A+7
:962   const bool claimed_range_attempted = (block + 1 >= advertised); // needs b >= claim-1
:963   if(!claimed_range_attempted) { ...; continue; }                 // BELOW the claim: keeps going
```

Below the advertised count the trip falls through to `continue` at `:970` - that is the advertised-count floor doing its job - so a run of eight does **not** end the sweep there. Both conditions must hold, which makes the last block attempted

    L = max(A + 7, claim - 1)

and therefore

    reaches 56  <=>  A >= 49  OR  claim >= 57
    reaches 57  <=>  A >= 50  OR  claim >= 58

"a card silent from block A is attempted through A+7" is only the first term. Worked cases:

| A | claim | L | reaches 56 | this comment says |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 50 | 49 | no | no |
| **0** | **57** | **56** | **yes** | **no** |
| 0 | 60 | 59 | yes | no |
| 49 | 49 | 56 | yes | yes |
| 40 | 56 | 55 | no | no |

So a card that answers no read at all but advertises 57 or more blocks does reach 56/57, three WRITE BLOCKs go out at each, and this paragraph says it cannot happen. That is the wrong direction on the one path where the UID check never runs.

Two smaller things in the same passage:

- `:1256` says the pair "ride together only when a **write** LANDS and resets the run". A landing **read** resets it too - `wipe_note_present` is called from the read-success path at `:932` and from the re-probe at `:1013`, neither of which increments `wiped`. So inside the `wiped == 0` branch the run genuinely can have been reset. "when a block ANSWERS" matches your own `:1253` framing of "blocks answer nothing".
- `CHANGELOG.md:72-73` has the same rule wrong in the opposite corner: "only one that both claims fewer than 49 blocks and stops answering above that claim stays short" misses a card claiming 20 that goes silent at block 50 (A=50, so it reaches 56/57 despite claiming well under 49).

This sentence has now been wrong in four consecutive rounds, each time in a new place. I would state the closed form once, here, and have the CHANGELOG carry only the qualitative half that cannot be wrong - "a card that keeps answering reads walks past 56/57 whatever it claims; otherwise it depends on where the silence starts and what the card claims, see the poller". The clock exit you added in `a27d187d` is correct and sits on top of all of it.

`0bd82c19` scoped the in-band error code correctly in one place and left it general in two.

`:41`, after the re-measurement:

> On the ST LRi2K that refusal is IN BAND (error 0x10, block not available); on the other two the client reported a failure that does not separate an error frame from silence, **so "the registers answer" is one chip**.

Still stated as a property of armed cards generally:

- **here, `:855`** - "with error 0x10, so the sweep reaches commit and is turned away rather than clearing it"
- `:339` - "assumed: on an armed card the 62/63 writes come back REFUSED (error 0x10) and the UID moves"

Before the re-measurement "an armed card" meant the single LRi2K and both read correctly. Now the file says one thing at `:41` and a wider thing at these two.

`:855` is the load-bearing one: the OPEN QUESTION's conclusion - that an armed card stays armed while its UID moves - rests on the commit write being refused rather than silently dropped, and the in-band evidence for that is one chip. "(error 0x10 on the LRi2K; see ISO15693_MAGIC_BLK_UNLOCK)" at both would close it.

A fact that was in exactly one place and is now in zero. `9b80e348` removed from this bullet:

> The four backdoor addresses are not memory: they answer no read at any point, so a card's advertised block count is its capacity and 56/57/62/63 are write-only registers sitting outside it.

I grepped the whole app - `magic/`, `scenes/`, `helpers/`, both headers and the CHANGELOG. Nothing at HEAD states that the backdoor addresses answer no read, or that they sit above the advertised count. The companion half of that same sentence, the UID taking effect immediately, did survive (`iso15693_poller.c:36-40`, `iso15693_poller.h:83`).

It is quietly load-bearing twice:

- it is why the 49-block threshold at `:1252` is about *overshoot* at all. 56/57 lying **above** a gen1 card's claim is what makes "how far past the claim does the sweep run" the question. Without it a reader cannot see why the claim matters rather than just the geometry.
- it explains the **"Wiped 58/58"** reproduction at `:857` on a card the same CHANGELOG describes as a 56-block LRi2K. Those two numbers only reconcile if 56/57 are outside the advertised count.

This is measured hardware behaviour that nothing else records, and it is not argumentation - it is the kind of fact the trim was supposed to keep. Worth restoring, in the poller rather than the release notes if you would rather the CHANGELOG stay lean.

Small correction to an invariant note - the conclusion holds, the count does not.

> the flag is set only inside Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe, **whose one exit is success_or_partial**

Two exits reach that point with `write_state == Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe`: the case body itself (`iso15693_poller.c:1406` sets the flag, `:1413` reports), and the activation-error path at `:1457-1469`, which tests `verifying_wipe` and also reports `success_or_partial` at `:1468` rather than falling through to the CardLost at `:1471`.

Both are `success_or_partial`, so the invariant this note exists to pin - a CardLost result always carries `uid_verified` false - is if anything better supported than the note claims: no CardLost can be emitted once that state is entered at all, by either route.

Keeping the defensive term with the reasoning written out is the right call, and the answer to my round-10 note is a good one. Just "whose exits are both success_or_partial".

Pre-existing tension the trim would have been the moment to settle, since both lines were rewritten this round.

`:42` says an over-capacity clone copies the blocks that do fit **"exactly"**.
`:55` says **"Block contents are not compared - a data block counts as written when the card acknowledges it."**

Thirteen lines apart, and the second is the one the code supports. "exactly" promises a verification the clone does not perform. The pre-trim wording ("clones faithfully") had the same problem, so this is not new - but "every block the card acknowledged" would say what actually happened and cost nothing.
